sentences.text: Long ago, a mother named Rosa lived with her daughter, Pinang.
Pinang was very lazy.
She always asked, "Where are my clothes? Where is my food?"
One day, the mother became very sick.
She asked her daughter to cook rice.
But Pinang would not look around the kitchen.
She shouted, "Mother, where is the pot?"
The mother whispered, "I hope you grow many eyes to look around."
Soon, Pinang disappeared, and in her place grew a fruit with many eyes.

comprehension_questions.stem: Who lived in the small house?
What was the daughter like?
What did the mother ask the daughter to cook?
Where could the daughter not find anything?
What did the mother whisper to her daughter?
comprehension_questions.correct: "I hope you grow many eyes to look around."

comprehension_questions.stem: What happened to the daughter at the end of the story?
comprehension_questions.correct: She disappeared and became a fruit.

comprehension_questions.stem: Why did the mother wish her daughter had many eyes?
comprehension_questions.correct: Because the daughter could not see what she needed to do.
distractors: Because the mother wanted a pet.
Because the mother was angry at the world.

comprehension_questions.stem: What does the story teach us?
comprehension_questions.correct: We should help our parents and not be lazy.
distractors: We should live in a small house.

sentences.text: One morning, a monkey and a turtle walked together in the forest.
The monkey saw a banana tree and said, "Let us plant this tree."
The monkey took the top part with leaves.
The turtle took the bottom part with roots.
The monkey laughed and said, "My part is better!"
But soon, the turtle's part grew into a big tree with sweet bananas.
The monkey's part died.
The monkey asked the turtle for some bananas.
The turtle said, "Climb the tree, but do not eat too much."
The greedy monkey climbed, ate many bananas, and fell down.
The turtle smiled and said, "Slow and steady is better than greedy and fast."

comprehension_questions.stem: Where did the monkey and the turtle walk together?
What tree did the monkey see?
Which part did the monkey take?
Which part did the turtle take?
What grew from the turtle's part of the tree?
comprehension_questions.correct: A big tree with sweet bananas

comprehension_questions.stem: What happened to the monkey's part?
What did the monkey ask the turtle for?
Why did the monkey fall from the tree?
comprehension_questions.correct: Because he was greedy and ate too much.
distractors: Because the tree was too tall.

comprehension_questions.stem: What lesson does the story teach us?
comprehension_questions.correct: Being patient is better than being greedy.

comprehension_questions.stem: Why did the monkey laugh at the turtle at first?
comprehension_questions.correct: He thought his part of the tree was better.
distractors: He wanted to play a game.

comprehension_questions.stem: How would you describe the monkey in this story?
What does the turtle mean by slow and steady is better than greedy and fast?
comprehension_questions.correct: Patience leads to better results than rushing for more

sentences.text: Long ago, in a village near the mountains, lived a kind farmer named Mang Isko.
He had one daughter, Manggita, who loved helping the poor.
Every day, she gave rice to hungry neighbors.
One year, a terrible drought came.
The river dried up, and the crops died.
Many villagers became weak and sad.
Manggita prayed every night for her people.
One evening, a strange light appeared in her garden.
A tree grew where the light touched the ground.
It bore golden fruit shaped like a heart.
The villagers ate the fruit and felt strong again.
They named the tree "mangga" after Manggita, the beloved girl who saved them all.

comprehension_questions.stem: Where did Mang Isko live?
comprehension_questions.correct: In a village near the mountains

comprehension_questions.stem: What was the name of Mang Isko's daughter?
What did Manggita give to hungry neighbors?
What disaster came to the village?
What happened to the river and crops?
comprehension_questions.correct: The river dried up and the crops died.

comprehension_questions.stem: What did Manggita do every night?
Where did the strange light appear?
What shape was the fruit?
Why did the villagers name the tree after Manggita?
comprehension_questions.correct: Because she loved and saved them.

comprehension_questions.stem: Why did Manggita pray every night?
comprehension_questions.correct: She wanted to help her people who were suffering.
distractors: She was afraid of the dark.

comprehension_questions.stem: What kind of person was Manggita?
Why did the villagers feel strong again?
comprehension_questions.correct: They ate the fruit from the magical tree.
distractors: They moved to a new village.

comprehension_questions.stem: What does this story teach us about helping others?
comprehension_questions.correct: Helping others with a kind heart can be rewarded in unexpected ways.
distractors: Never share your food with neighbors.
Only help people who can pay you back.
Praying is more important than acting.

comprehension_questions.stem: Why do you think the author wrote this story?
comprehension_questions.correct: To explain where mangoes come from and to teach kindness.
distractors: To make people afraid of droughts.
To describe a real farmer's life.
To sell more mangoes in the market.

words.lesson_cue: This is a legend... L, E, G, E, N, D... Legend!

words.sample_sentence: The hungry boy asks Nanay for rice.

words.lesson_cue: This is a mother... M, O, T, H, E, R... Mother!

words.sample_sentence: Mother cooks dinner for our family.

words.lesson_cue: This is a daughter... D, A, U, G, H, T, E, R... Daughter!

words.sample_sentence: The daughter helps her mother at home.

words.lesson_cue: This is kindness... K, I, N, D, N, E, S, S... Kindness!

words.sample_sentence: Her kindness makes everyone smile.

words.sample_sentence: The patient girl waits for her turn.

words.lesson_cue: This is gentle... G, E, N, T, L, E... Gentle!

words.lesson_cue: This is helpful... H, E, L, P, F, U, L... Helpful!

words.sample_sentence: The helpful boy carries the heavy bag.

quiz_questions.stem: Which word means "always ready to help"?

words.lesson_cue: This is grateful... G, R, A, T, E, F, U, L... Grateful!
words.definition: Feeling thankful for something.
words.sample_sentence: We are grateful for our family.

words.lesson_cue: This is a community... C, O, M, M, U, N, I, T, Y... Community!
words.definition: A group of people living in the same place.

words.lesson_cue: This is a neighbor... N, E, I, G, H, B, O, R... Neighbor!

words.lesson_cue: This is unity... U, N, I, T, Y... Unity!

words.lesson_cue: This is together... T, O, G, E, T, H, E, R... Together!

words.sample_sentence: The family eats dinner together.

words.lesson_cue: This is share... S, H, A, R, E... Share!

words.sample_sentence: Please share your baon with your friend.

words.lesson_cue: This is cooperate... C, O, O, P, E, R, A, T, E... Cooperate!
words.definition: To work together for the same goal.
words.sample_sentence: We cooperate to clean the classroom.

words.lesson_cue: This is a harvest... H, A, R, V, E, S, T... Harvest!

words.lesson_cue: This is generous... G, E, N, E, R, O, U, S... Generous!

words.lesson_cue: This is a volunteer... V, O, L, U, N, T, E, E, R... Volunteer!

words.lesson_cue: This is climate... C, L, I, M, A, T, E... Climate!

words.lesson_cue: This is weather... W, E, A, T, H, E, R... Weather!

words.lesson_cue: This is a drought... D, R, O, U, G, H, T... Drought!

quiz_questions.stem: Which word means "a long time with no rain"?

words.lesson_cue: This is commitment... C, O, M, M, I, T, M, E, N, T... Commitment!
